title: surrey-biome-pipeline: a two-extent test of scale-free climate downscaling against polygon-scale water stress

creators.name: Wang, Joshua
creators.affiliation: Fraser Heights Secondary, Surrey, British Columbia, Canada

description:
Code, method and applied output for a controlled test of whether high-resolution "scale-free" downscaled climate data (ClimateBC) predicts polygon-scale vegetation water stress better than the same variables degraded to a coarse regional-model grid.

The test was run at two spatial extents. Over the City of Surrey's 153 Green Infrastructure Network corridors it was inconclusive for structural reasons: coarsening to 4 km removed only 12.3% of the predictors' spatial variance, and the climate predictors varied mostly between years while water stress varied mostly between corridors. Repeated on a 100 km Fraser Valley elevation transect spanning 4-1,920 m (300 forest stands x 4 summers), the contrast became measurable (48.4% of spatial variance removed at 25 km) and the result reversed: the coarse model significantly outperformed the scale-free one, with the paired confidence interval excluding zero at two cell sizes and in 32 of 32 random seeds. Neither model reached usable skill. Stand water stress proved near-orthogonal to the macroclimate gradient; only local terrain and stand structure reached positive cross-validated skill.

The repository also contains the applied deliverable built after the resolution approach was shown not to work: CDEI, a Sentinel-2 and Landsat index of polygon water stress, mapped and ranked across Surrey's corridors and checked independently against Sentinel-1 radar and against ClimateBC moisture variables.

Pipeline modules under src/pipeline/ each expose an importable API and a command-line entry point; walkthrough notebooks under notebooks/ reproduce each stage end to end. All randomness is seeded (seed 26910). Source data are public and are not redistributed here; every input is regenerable from the pipeline.

A manuscript describing this work is in preparation for a preprint server. It has not been posted, submitted or peer reviewed.
notes: Generative AI tools were used in preparing this work and are disclosed in the accompanying manuscript: they were used to scaffold code and draft technical prose, which the author then revised, and as an adversarial reviewer of drafted sections.
